correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 40–61. At most three sites cannot cover the eleven differences. A four-site cover allocates six unordered pairs to five classes with multiplicities (2,1,1,1,1). If θ is the cross-phase at the repeated shift, the two equal terms give (1/2)|cos((θ−2πb(r−u)/11)/2)|. Since r−u≠0, the eleven angles form a rotated regular eleven-gon, and the largest possible distance from π to the nearest angle is π/11, attained exactly when π is a midpoint. Odd order makes that equivalent to θ being a multiple of 2π/11. The opposite shift has the same magnitudes; singleton shifts are 1/4, and at zero shift b≠0 the pair count gives (3+2cos(2πbδ/11))/16 for the squared magnitude, at least 1/16. Thus the optimal value and all equality conditions hold; {0,1,2,5} is a cover. In the taper, the repeated-shift term magnitudes are 21/83 and 9/83, the smallest singleton product is 12/83, and the zero-shift bound is (49−34)/83. Hence the exact margin is 12/83, greater than sin(π/22) by sin(π/22)<1/7<12/83. The Weyl basis and orthogonal character images give singular values √11|A_g| with largest √11, establishing both full-lifting condition numbers. No claim of weighted optimality is made. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; it samples no continuum of phases, and the proof does not rely on it.

value.rationale: Eleven is a natural minimally supported test: four sites are necessary and there is precisely one repeated unoriented difference in a cover. The continuum phase classification and exact smallest-singular-value barrier distinguish injectivity from stable inversion. A same-support amplitude taper more than doubles the margin, demonstrating a genuine limitation of a natural design constraint, not just a numerical improvement over a single flat-phase example.
